Given my preference ordering (x > w > z > y), I should rank x as my first choice because it is my most preferred school. Although I have a lower priority at x (priority 2) compared to w and y (priority 1), the fact that most applicants favor y > x > w > z means there might be less competition for x than for y. Therefore, I might have a good chance of being accepted by x.

For my second choice, I should rank w because it is my second most preferred school, and I have the highest priority there (priority 1). This increases my chances of being accepted if I am rejected by x.

For my third choice, I should rank z. While it is my third preference, I have a priority of 2 there, which could give me a reasonable chance of acceptance if both x and w reject me.

Finally, I should rank y last. Despite having the highest priority at y (priority 1), it is my least preferred school. Additionally, since most applicants favor y, the competition will likely be intense, which could make it harder to secure a spot even with high priority.

In summary, my strategy is to rank schools according to my true preferences, as the deferred acceptance algorithm will ensure the best possible match given my priorities and the preferences of other students.
